svg.title: The client reports contractions every 8-10 minutes for 3 hours that have not gotten stronger, and they ease after walking around the unit. Cervical exam is unchanged at 1 cm/50% effaced on two checks 1 hour apart. FHR is 140/min with moderate variability.
svg.desc: Unchanged cervical dilation and effacement despite hours of contractions, along with contractions that ease with ambulation, are hallmarks of false labor; true labor produces progressive cervical change that does not resolve with activity. Discharge teaching with instructions to return if the pattern changes is appropriate here, while tocolytics and oxytocin are not needed since there is no evidence of preterm or dysfunctional labor. Ongoing monitoring should focus on cervical dilation/effacement and the contraction pattern, since those two findings are what distinguish true from false labor; temperature and reflexes are not relevant to this presentation.
